issues.description: The solution repository's PersonService class declares a constructor with a single Object parameter (public PersonService(Object personRepository)), whereas the template (and the problem statement) expect a no-argument constructor for PersonService. The problem statement explicitly warns 'Do not change the attributes of PersonService' and asks students to implement sorting inside PersonService. Changing the constructor signature is a structural mismatch: it prevents Spring from instantiating PersonService as an uncomplicated @Service bean (no matching Object bean will be available for autowiring) and diverges from the template students start with. This would confuse students and can break the application wiring, making it impossible to run the server or to follow the intended implementation steps.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore a no-argument constructor for PersonService (matching the template and the problem intent). Replace the incorrect constructor 'public PersonService(Object personRepository) { this.persons = new ArrayList<>(); }' with 'public PersonService() { this.persons = new ArrayList<>(); }'. This keeps the service as a simple Spring-managed bean and preserves the instructional contract that students should not change the service's attributes.

issues.description: PersonService constructor signature differs between template and solution. The problem statement and template expect/contain a no-argument PersonService constructor that initializes the internal persons list, and the problem explicitly warns not to change PersonService attributes. The solution repository instead provides a constructor with a parameter (public PersonService(Object personRepository) { ... }). This constructor-parameter mismatch is not discussed in the problem statement and is likely an unintended divergence. It will confuse students mapping the required PersonService (no-arg) to the provided solution (parameterized), may interfere with Spring dependency wiring in examples, and increases extraneous cognitive load when students try to compare template and solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore consistent PersonService constructor across artifacts. Change the solution's constructor to a no-argument constructor that initializes the persons list (e.g. public PersonService() { this.persons = new ArrayList<>(); }) so it matches the template and the problem statement note. Alternatively, if a parameterized constructor is intended, update the problem statement and template to document and use the same constructor signature consistently.
